Factions_Blue_Goals: Find what is lost, understand what is unexplained, and remember what is forgotten. The mystery is what motivates the Vanguard to search deeper and deeper. There is no greater priority for them. Until we find the truth and discover what has been forgotten, we will never find our true selves. And without that, we are nobody. Why do we need riches, or a long prosperous life, if we don't understand anything? History is the key to our future.
Factions_Blue_Methods: Immersed in old libraries and archives, filled with the desire to find all the remnants of the Old World. They bravely venture into even the most dangerous regions, as they feel it's their destiny to explore. They are not afraid, and they do not withdraw. She guides them. They trust her. They pray, and go on another difficult expedition. How many will come back this time? It does not matter. This is the price of discovery.
Factions_Blue_PublicOpinion: There are various rumors about the Vanguard. Whoever joins them changes forever. Some are afraid of them, or consider them fanatics who commit terrible acts in the name of knowledge. But there are two sides to every coin. Thanks to their research, we have a chance to learn more about the terrifying world around us. Maybe one day, we’ll even understand it, and learn to live in harmony with it. Or perhaps, we may even find a way to stop the Blightstorm?
Factions_Blue_Relationships: They venture into any ruins they can find, looking for ancient artifacts and relics. They’ll refuse to share their knowledge, unless you can offer them something in return. This attitude creates a strenuous relationship between the factions. Most of the time, however, the Vanguard pretends to be neutral... Until something angers them.
Factions_Green_Goals: For the First Dawn Company, the two most important things in life are social standing and wealth. They like to establish settlements close to fertile lands, where they can quickly produce food in enormous quantities. Thanks to this tactic, they control the production and distribution of food throughout the realm. If you don’t take care of your supply chains quickly, you’ll soon be completely dependent on them.
Factions_Green_Methods: It's all about the money. The First Dawn Company are ruthless materialists, who trade not only in resources or food, but sometimes even in people too. Nothing will stop them if there's profit to be made.
Factions_Green_Motto: “No bees, no honey; no work, no money”
Factions_Green_PublicOpionion: On one hand, it might seem that the First Dawn Company only thinks about profit - but on the other, without them, we would face an economic crisis. It's not easy to travel in a merchant's cart down dangerous valleys, so people are grateful for the First Dawn's logistical prowess.
Factions_Green_Relationships: It does not go unnoticed by the other factions that the First Dawn Company gladly endows the Queen with riches to win her favor. However, it's unknown if this tactic will win them her trust in the long run.
Factions_Orange_Goals: Innovators, pioneers, people of progress. They have only one goal: to tame the storm. Tame it, and use its potential for the benefit of all people. That's why their specialization lies in creating Rainpunk technology. Advanced machines, durable tools, workshops and shelters, even eternal bonfires - all are their creations. Whatever will they surprise us with next?
Factions_Orange_Methods: People of ambition and diligence. They will not rest until they prove to everyone (and above all, to the Queen) that they are the best engineers in the realm. They’re not looking for fame or riches. Their reward is simply in their sense of security, and the gratitude of all species.
Factions_Orange_PublicOpinion: Adored by many, but hated by some. Most people are eternally grateful for their toil and hard work, but some despise their creations. Most religious groups fear that the Brass Order will bring doom upon the kingdom by mindlessly exploiting the natural environment. It's said that some settlements have already fallen due to the Curse of the Forest, brought about by the Brass Order's machines. Survivors warn, and remember...
Factions_Orange_Relationships: The Brass Order works well with the First Dawn Company, but they are in eternal conflict with the Vanguard of the Stolen Keys. Their visions and mindsets are complete polar opposites. The question is not "if" this conflict will escalate, but rather "when".

GameAlerts_CompletedTimedOrders_Descript: Timed orders have to be delivered before the time runs out!
GameAlerts_DangerousGladeTooSoon_Descrip: Your settlement is not yet prepared for the threats that can be found in Dangerous Glades! Unmark the trees leading to the Dangerous Glade, and follow your orders for now.
GameAlerts_DeadlyHostility_Description: High Hostility of the Forest during the storm will crush your people's Resolve. To lower Hostility, unassign woodcutters, sacrifice fuel in the Ancient Hearth, or build additional hearths. Check the hostility icon on the upper HUD to read more about Hostility sources.
GameAlerts_LowFire_Description: The fire in your main Hearth is going out! Without it, your villagers' Resolve will fall drastically!
GameAlerts_LowFood_Description: Your villagers will eat anything, if necessary, but with no food at all they will starve. Build new food production buildings, or assign workers to existing ones.
GameAlerts_LowFuel_Description: The village needs fuel (wood, coal, oil) for the Hearth. Build more Woodcutters' Camps and assign more woodcutters.
GameAlerts_LowResolve_Description: To increase the Resolve of a given species, provide food they like, meet their needs, and build houses. You can also invest in perks and effects that will boost their Resolve.
GameAlerts_Newcomers_Description: Once in a while, you can welcome a new group of villagers. Don't let them wait too long!
GameAlerts_NewOrders_Description: Periodically, you’ll be assigned new orders from the Citadel. Select the envelope icon in the upper right corner to check the new objectives.
GameAlerts_NoBlackMarket_Desc: You won't last long in these harsh lands without a Black Market. Build one to gain access to resource deals.
GameAlerts_NoBuilders_Description: Only villagers who aren't assigned to a building can build structures. Press {0} on a worker's portrait in the building panel to make them a builder.
GameAlerts_NoCompletedOrders_Description: The Queen gave you orders - keep track of them and try to complete them to advance your settlement.
GameAlerts_NoDeposits_Description: This building needs a gathering node to continue working. It either doesn't have access to one or is located too far from one to be efficient.
GameAlerts_NoFarmfields_Description: Farmers can only plant crops on farm fields that have been built on fertile soil.
GameAlerts_NoFirekeeper_Description: Without a firekeeper assigned to the Main Hearth, the fire will die out, and your villagers will perish.
GameAlerts_NoLakes_Description: This building needs a fishing pond to continue working. It either doesn't have access to one, or has insufficient bait to continue.
GameAlerts_NoLumberCamp_Description: To survive, the village needs a constant supply of wood. Build a Woodcutters' Camp.
GameAlerts_NoNaturalResources_Descriptio: There are no trees suitable for felling within the building's area. Move the Woodcutters' Camp closer to the forest, or change the camp's settings.
GameAlerts_NoOre_Description: A mine has depleted all of its available veins. Demolish it and look for new mining veins in nearby glades.
GameAlerts_NoOre_UpgradeAvailableDescrip: A mine has depleted all of its available veins. You can upgrade it to reach lower levels and gain access to more mining veins.
GameAlerts_NoParts_Description: Parts are required to build camps and expand the village. Salvage unused camps, or venture into the wilds to acquire this rare resource.
GameAlerts_NoTreesMarked_Description: To cut through the forest and reach glades faster, you can mark certain trees for felling. Select the axe icon on the right-hand side of the lower HUD, and drag the pointer over the trees.
GameAlerts_NoWoodcutters_Description: To survive, the village needs a constant supply of wood. Assign at least 4 workers to your Woodcutters' Camps.
GameAlerts_PoroFull_Desc: The Fluffbeak's pasture is full of manure.
GameAlerts_ReputationRewards_Description: You can choose a new blueprint as a reward for earning Reputation Points. Press the pulsing number on the reputation bar at the bottom of the screen.
GameAlerts_RoadsDestroyed_Alert_Descript: All your roads have been destroyed due to flooding caused by: Rain Spirit Totem
GameAlerts_SealPlague_Desc: The Ancient Seal is crumbling, releasing a new plague every storm. {0}: {1}
GameAlerts_SeasonRewards_Description: From time to time, the Queen will offer you powerful cornerstones. Select the Queen's Mask icon in the top right corner of the screen.
GameAlerts_Starvation_Description: {1} ({0}) are so starved, they will die if they don't eat during their next break.
GameAlerts_TooManyTreesMarked_Descriptio: Forest exploration is essential, and marking too many trees can slow you down. Use the axe icon with the minus sign on the right hand side of the lower HUD to unselect marked trees.
GameAlerts_UnresolvedRelics_Description: You can interact with objects found in the forest. Allocate resources, assign workers, choose rewards, and give orders to investigate.
GameAlerts_UnseenRelics_Description: Woodcutters have discovered a new dangerous event in the forest!
GameAlerts_UnstartedRelics_Description: An event found in the forest has workers assigned, but no orders to investigate were given.
GameAlerts_UpcomingPayment_Description: One or more of your payments is due next season.
GameUI_AchievementTooltip_Desc: Completing this deed will also reward you with an achievement.
GameUI_AltarPanel_Inactive_Description: The priestess will only arrive during the storm, and only after you acquire an Altar Activation charge from earning <color=#e0e09f>Reputation</color>.
GameUI_AltarPanel_NPC_Description: "Gythe'th bless you, outsider. For a small fee, I can grant you unimaginable power... far greater than any boon the false queen can offer you."
GameUI_Archaeologist_NextLevel_Tooltip_D: To buy an upgrade, you need to meet the requirements. The necessary resources can be changed to other resources by selecting the resource icon. Once an upgrade has been purchased, it cannot be refunded or exchanged for another.
GameUI_Archaeologist_Upgrades_Tooltip_De: In the Archaeologist's Office, you can buy upgrades that reveal the location of an excavation site or aid exploration. The first upgrade is available for free. Only one upgrade can be purchased per row.
GameUI_BatsShrine_Abilities_Tooltip_Desc: Choose a species to punish. One of its members will leave the settlement, permanently increasing the productivity of all workers.
GameUI_BlackMarketOffersTooltip_Desc: The Syndicate has updated its offers since you last checked.
GameUI_BlackMarketPopup_CreditButton_Des: The loan must be repaid within 3 seasons (by the start of {0} in year {1}), or the Syndicate will kidnap {2} villagers.
GameUI_BlackMarketPopup_CreditRating_Bad: According to Zhera's calculations, the interest rate on this offer is a ripoff.
GameUI_BlackMarketPopup_CreditRating_Goo: According to Zhera's calculations, the interest rate on this offer is favorable.
